cells.Title: Already-compressed list and 7-Zip storage
cells.Detail: One list, defined in exactly one place, names the file extensions known to be already compressed (archives, disk images, video, audio, image and packed-container formats). It is the accepted-known-formats fast path, not an attempt at completeness: office and text formats are not on it because they are not known to be already compressed, and a filesystem container such as .iso is excluded because listing it would wrongly call its contents compressed. Its answer is an input to the storage-form decision (LLR-086), taken as if compression were enabled so it carries only the list's opinion; it is the whole decision only with the probe off or below the probe's size floor. The engine holds no copy of the list; it asks the shared library. The user-facing documentation's table of already-compressed extensions is kept equal to the live list. Writing a compressed object first removes any existing object at the destination name, because the archiver adds to an existing archive rather than replacing it: the write path trusts only the index, so an unreferenced object at that content-derived name (left by a run killed before its index was written, by a row evicted while its object awaits prune, or by an interrupted archiver) would otherwise be merged into the new object. The archive is written at the 7-Zip compression level resolved once from FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL (LLR-037), 9 unless the operator sets otherwise. The shared library publishes the resolved level and any rejected raw value, so the entry point can refuse an invalid value without reaching into the library's internal state, and the library still depends on nothing in the engine.

cells.Title: Stale staging: classify, reclaim or refuse
cells.Detail: A run that finds a staging area already present under the change root never overwrites it. Creating the staging area is the fast path and is unchanged for a healthy run; classification is reached only when the create fails and the staging area exists as a directory, and any other create failure is logged verbatim and re-raised. Classification takes a forced, literal, fail-closed listing of the staging area and the owner record (LLR-080), and on the Empty and OwnerStale verdicts the caller takes the confirmation sample itself, so the classifier stays pure. The confirmation wait is at least 90 s, lengthened to the record's own declared heartbeat cadence plus 30 s, and capped at 600 s. Only a confirmed-stale area is reclaimed, by this exact protocol: move it aside to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>; re-examine the moved folder against the sampled identity, and if it is live move it straight back and refuse; create a fresh staging area and immediately write this run's owner record, closing the reclaimer's own create-to-marker window; then re-list the aside folder, delete only the exact marker by name, and delete the folder non-recursively. Nothing in this path deletes recursively; if either delete fails the folder is kept and the documented recovery is printed, and a failed move refuses without retrying in a loop. Every other verdict refuses with its own token: [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused], [SR-075/prune-held]; Indeterminate, or a staging area that is a reparse point, refuses with the content token. The refusal message states its reason without hedging. On success the run writes its owner record as soon as the staging area exists and keeps a rooted heartbeat handle with it. All work after acquisition runs inside a guard that always stops and drains the heartbeat, so an exception after the staging area gains content cannot leave a live heartbeat advertising an abandoned lock as owned; that guard only stops the heartbeat and deletes nothing. A run cleans up its own staging area only after proving the area is still its own: the marker is present and carries this run's id, and nothing is inside beyond the marker and this run's own early staging artifacts (the copied prior index, its witness and the directory sidecar, none of them a unique copy, which is what lets a late capacity refusal release its own lock instead of stranding the staging area). It then stops and drains the heartbeat, deletes those exact leaves by name with the marker last, and removes the folder non-recursively; on any doubt it keeps the folder and logs [SR-075/lock-lost]. Either way the original error is re-raised. This prevents a resurrected owner's ordinary failure from recursively deleting its successor's staging area. The run re-reads the marker and compares the run id at five boundaries: before writing the staging copy of the index, before evicting removed files, before preserving superseded data, before publishing the backup root's index and witness, and before publishing the snapshot. An unreadable marker is retried three times about 300 ms apart; a mismatch is never retried and aborts the run, cleaning up nothing. Immediately before the snapshot is published the run stops and drains the heartbeat and removes its marker, because publishing either deletes the staging area or turns it wholesale into a snapshot, and a surviving marker would be published into every snapshot and then refused by prune's unreferenced-data rail (SR-046). The whole create, classification, confirmation sample and any reclaim run under the staging OS lock (LLR-090), taken before the staging area is touched; a lock that cannot be taken refuses the set first. The held lock is passed to classification and reclaim only to be logged: every verdict and refusal above is unchanged by it, because an older FileBackup takes no OS lock. The lock is released when staging setup fails, or at the very end after the heartbeat is stopped, never before the snapshot is published.

cells.Detail: The index writer publishes the index atomically (SR-082, LLR-087) and then writes its witness: the XXH128 digest of the written index, emitted as Version/Rows/Bytes/XxH128/Written key=value lines, UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, written to a temporary sidecar in the same folder and published by an atomic rename over any prior witness. cells.Detail: A shared-library verifier reads the witness, compares Bytes, Rows and XxH128 against the index on disk, and returns a verdict (Verified, Absent, Mismatch or Malformed) with the failing field and an optional non-fatal warning. Fields are checked Bytes, then Rows, then XxH128, but a Rows-only disagreement defers to the digest: when bytes and digest match, the index IS the witnessed one, so it verifies with a warning (counting-semantics divergence) rather than aborting; with no digest present, a row-count disagreement still aborts. Both restorers verify after confirming the index exists and before creating the target folder, the restore log or running the capacity pre-check, so an exit-2 or exit-3 refusal writes nothing into the target (log lines are buffered and flushed once the log exists). The PowerShell restorer also checks the index's CSV header shape, as the shell restorer already does, and the shell restorer verifies at the same point, immediately after its header check. cells.Detail: The pool locator in both restorers returns one cause per lookup: Found, ContentMissing, DependencyMissing or StorageUnreadable, with a detail. Search folders are probed for existence and readability. An archive candidate met without a usable 7-Zip yields DependencyMissing; a candidate that cannot be read at all is the host condition StorageUnreadable and records exactly that one cause, never DependencyMissing as well; a candidate that fails to expand is data damage, folded into the ContentMissing detail (' ; N candidate(s) could not be expanded: <first>'). The locator never returns CandidateError. Whether an expand failure counts as damage is gated by a self-test that 7-Zip is actually usable. The restore loop records each unrestored row with its cause and detail; its own CandidateError (the row's own file failed to expand or copy) and WriteMismatch stay host-class. The summary classifies unrestored rows into the content class (exit 1) and the host class (exit 4). Both restorers report an unlistable snapshot tree as StorageUnreadable (exit 4) rather than silently shrinking the recovery pool. Under -ExitCode (which the Windows launcher passes) a classified outcome becomes the process exit code; otherwise it raises an error carrying the same message wording, so in-process callers keep working. Any terminating error the restorer did not classify is routed to the precondition class (exit 2 under -ExitCode, re-raised otherwise), so an unexpected failure can never be reported as data loss (1). Failures creating the target folder or the restore log route through the same class, matching the shell restorer's refusal (2) for a file occupying the target path. The shell restorer reports usage and precondition failures as 2, the witness refusal as 3, and the 1-versus-4 split at the end of its run; its usage text and header comment carry the exit-code table (SR-040).

cells.Detail: The configuration loader belongs to the backup-only engine, not the shared library, because configuration loading has no restore-side meaning and the library must stay restore-safe. It accepts the JSON and the CLIXML configuration document, chosen by file extension. JSON: ConfigVersion must be an integer within [1, the current schema version], range-checked before any integer conversion, so an out-of-range version is refused as unsupported rather than by luck of fractional representation. The key set is closed at the top level, under Tools, under Secrets and in each set, and Secrets.Credential is refused explicitly. Type checks read the parsed JSON value's actual type, so a quoted "false" is refused rather than coerced to true; an 'integer' accepts any integral-valued JSON number, culture-safely and including one beyond the 64-bit range. CLIXML: the shape check only, keeping its established message wording. Both formats run the same shape and value checks. Defaults are materialised for every set: SourceStatePath defaults to SourcePath, AllowEmptySource to false, CompressProbe to always, and HashRecalcFreq is upper-cased. Every validated optional key reaches the engine; a validated key must never be silently dropped during defaulting. CompressProbe's vocabulary is exact lowercase (off, excluded-extensions, always), so a mixed-case 'Always' is refused, and the value check runs for both formats, which makes it the only place an invalid CLIXML value is caught. Errors are terminating, single, first in document order, and name the JSON path; a set is named by its real array index. A published draft-07 JSON schema with additionalProperties:false mirrors the validator, including the CompressProbe enum, the BackupSets shape and the ConfigVersion constant. It is documentation, not read at runtime, and is not shipped in the container image. ConfigVersion stays 2 for an optional, defaulted key: such an addition is additive (SR-063). The key is documented in the entry point's help and example configuration, the README field table and IF-001 (SR-042).

cells.Detail: The prune plan builds the pool's content index (LLR-047) and derives the demand set: every row outside the target whose DataPath is blank, or whose non-blank DataPath names a file that is absent (verification can blank root DataPaths in a damaged store). It emits one plan item per endangered key, naming its source location and row, its destination folder, name and row, its stored form and its bytes. The destination is elected as cross-change deduplication elects it: the backup root when it demands the key, otherwise the newest demanding snapshot by folder order. The destination name IS the source row's DataPath: a stored object's name derives from its content and stored form, so a re-homed object's name is always identical to its source's. A name that would classify as root-level infrastructure at the destination, or that would overwrite a DIFFERENT file already there, is recorded as a code-2 problem instead of an item; an identical file already there is treated as an interrupted prune's completed copy, and the prune resumes. A re-homed copy is written to '<destination>.fbprune.tmp', path taken literally, and verified for stored-form identity (length and XXH128 equal to the source) and, unless content verification is skipped, for content identity against the row's xxH2Hash and Length, expanding an archive to a temporary file first, the same check the restorers' pool locator makes. It is then published by rename. Publishing the plan mutates only DataPath, Compressed and StoredAsHashSize on the destination row and persists through the one index writer, so the witness (SR-038) is re-stamped by its one writer and is never copied between folders.

cells.Detail: The prune precondition check returns the full set of refusals, each with a code, kind and message, rather than stopping at the first; the prune applies the precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1 over the whole set, and a -WhatIf run can report every refusal at once. It checks: - the target is an existing ^Snapshot_ folder that is a direct child of the resolved change root and contains no wildcard (2); - the SR-035 run-state gate: a malformed run-state record, or a populated backup index with no last-backup time (2); - no staging area in the change root (2, mutual exclusion with a backup, SR-017); - the plan's own code-2 problems (unknown target, infrastructure name, destination collision); - no unreferenced data files in the target, measured against the target's own index, unless -DiscardUnreferencedData (2); - the WHOLE pool resolves, so an already-broken pool or a pre-existing form disagreement refuses rather than being pruned into (2); - free space on each destination volume for the planned bytes, grouped by volume identity so a UNC or rooted POSIX store is checked too; an unmeasurable volume is skipped rather than refused (2); - 7-Zip present when the plan carries a compressed row and content verification is on (2); - the witness of EVERY pool index: Mismatch or Malformed (3), Absent (3) unless -AllowUnverifiedIndex. The pool-resolution check rebuilds the index over the pool minus an excluded folder and reports every row that would not resolve, plus every form disagreement: Compressed='Yes' with a located file that is not '.7z', or Compressed='No' with a located '.7z' file whose row's RelativePath is not itself '.7z' (which would be a legitimately stored already-compressed source file). Deletion renames the folder to 'Pruning_<name>', which is the commit point because that name matches neither the engine's snapshot pattern nor either restorer's ^Snapshot_ pattern, and then deletes it recursively. Residue is handled in two parts. Committed residue, 'Pruning_<that same name>' only, is removed before the named snapshot is planned: it is past the commit point, invisible to every consumer, and holds the name the plan needs; a host failure there is a code-4 record, not an unclassified error, and the step is skipped under -WhatIf. The entry sweep runs inside the transaction, after the rails pass and the staging lock is held, so a refusal mutates nothing and a sweep failure is code 4; it scans only pool folders (the backup root and Snapshot_*) and deletes a '*.fbprune.tmp' only when that folder's own index does not reference it, because a staged copy is unreferenced by construction while a referenced file is content. The prune takes the staging area by creating it without overwrite: creation is the atomic test, closing the window between the staging-busy rail and the lock; an existing folder becomes the staging-busy refusal (code 2), and cleanup never deletes a lock this invocation did not create. The PRUNE.inprogress marker is written inside the transaction.

cells.Detail: The content index maps each '<xxH2Hash>|<Length>' key to the locations holding those bytes, each recording its folder, DataPath, full path, whether it is the backup root, and its folder order: the backup root first, then the given snapshot folders in the order supplied (name order, oldest first). It skips blank DataPaths, blank hashes and rows whose file is not on disk: the index describes bytes that EXIST, so a blank row is demand and never supply. It also returns one record per indexed folder. By default each folder record carries only the folder's identity, order and the non-blank DataPath values of its index in index order, and no whole index is retained: each index is read once, fed to the map and dropped, so the content index's memory grows with the number of stored objects, not with the rows of every snapshot. A caller that needs whole rows asks for the indexes to be retained; the prune plan, the pool-resolution check and the storage-form audit do, so prune still holds whole indexes. Cross-change deduplication uses the lean default: duplicate election is unchanged, and it re-reads and rewrites only a change folder whose DataPaths name a vanished file (LLR-026); it derives its list of change indexes from the same pass. The snapshot inventory lists the change root's folders matching the one snapshot pattern every consumer uses, sorted by name, and parses each snapshot's point-in-time date from its folder name, tolerating the same-second disambiguating suffix. The reported physical, reclaimable and re-homed bytes of a snapshot come straight from the prune plan, so the reported reclaim is the achieved reclaim by construction.

cells.Detail: A stored file is classified as Archive or Raw from its first six bytes (the 7z signature 37 7A BC AF 27 1C) plus its extension, with no hashing. The storage-form audit walks the pool through the content index (LLR-047), the backup root first and then Snapshot_* in name order, and emits one finding per disagreement, naming the folder, RelativePath, DataPath, class, observed and expected form, and whether it is repairable. The classes are NameLies, FlagOverRaw, FlagOverArchive, DanglingDataPath, BlankRowFormDisagreement and Unreferenced. The already-compressed-source exemption is keyed on the payload, not the file name: when the observed form is Archive but the row says Compressed=No, the file's own bytes are hashed against the row's (xxH2Hash, Length); a match is correct raw storage of archive-shaped content and yields no finding, and only a mismatch is a genuine FlagOverArchive, because an already-compressed source can be named anything. A .7z RelativePath is the cheap fast path. The non-Deep scan widens that fast path for one shape only: a Compressed=No archive-signature object is exempt without hashing when all three hold: the row's RelativePath extension is one the already-compressed list exempts (asked of the shared library; the engine holds no copy of the list), its DataPath extension equals the row's RelativePath extension, and its on-disk length equals the row's Length. Without this, a store where a large share of objects are listed-format archives stored raw would be re-hashed in full on every non-Deep pass. The exemption proves form, not payload: a same-length substitution under a listed name passes the non-Deep scan and is caught by -Deep, the payload audit, which always hashes. An archive-signature object under a name the list does not exempt keeps the confirming hash. Otherwise the non-Deep scan reads six bytes per row. -Deep additionally verifies payload identity, and requires 7-Zip: a raw object by length and XXH128 against the row; an archive by its own bytes first, since for an already-compressed source stored raw those bytes ARE the payload, and only otherwise by expanding it to a temporary file and hashing. Repair acts only on findings whose evidence is a file in the row's own folder. It rewrites Compressed and renames the data file so name and form agree, never re-packs, never touches the six logical columns, and persists each folder through the one index writer. Findings are grouped by (folder, DataPath), so the physical rename happens once and every row referencing the old path adopts the observed form, including a row exempted by the payload-keyed rule, whose bytes' identity is read before the rename moves them (it follows the file and keeps its own Compressed). Blank-row findings are reported only. Enumeration recognises infrastructure only at each folder's own root (B6/SN-018). The outcome maps to the SR-040 table, and nothing in the backup run calls the audit. The verify entry point resolves the set's roots read-only, so verification creates no directory, does not require the source path, and reports a missing backup root as code 2. After a change to the already-compressed list or to the compression settings the pool can legitimately hold both forms of one (hash, length): content archived before the change and re-added raw after it. Cross-change deduplication keeps one copy and blanks the other snapshot row, whose recorded Compressed can then disagree with the surviving object; the resulting BlankRowFormDisagreement on that blanked row is expected and benign (reported only, never repaired), and restore is unaffected because both restorers decide the form from the file they locate.

cells.Detail: Free space is measured in the shared library, so the restore kit stays self-contained. The measurement resolves the path's containing volume from its full path, falls back to the drive for a drive-qualified path, and answers 'unknown' only when neither works; it never throws. Volume identity comes from the mount table: the longest real mount point that prefixes the resolved path on a separator boundary, so two paths on one POSIX mount (for example /backup and /backup/sub) are recognised as one volume. The PowerShell restorer's capacity check uses this, so SR-023 works for a rooted POSIX path. The backup capacity check sums the run's additions per volume: new (hash, length) groups the backup does not already hold, at uncompressed Length (a blank-DataPath row holds no bytes, so its heal copy is budgeted), plus the staging bytes only when the change root is on a different volume from the backup root. Demands on one volume are summed against that volume's free space, because checking them separately passed two demands that each fitted and together did not. A shortfall fails the set with a classified precondition failure (entry-point status 1) before any mutation: it is checked after the diff and before superseded data is preserved, the last point at which nothing has been written, so a refusal leaves none of this run's content written and no staging area orphaned. This is not a claim that the tree is byte-identical: nothing already stored is ever re-formed (SR-061), so there is nothing to migrate and nothing to size. An unmeasurable volume is skipped, not refused. There is no new configuration key (SR-042's schema is closed).

cells.Detail: The source walk, including hidden entries, records each directory that is EMPTY of files or carries a recorded attribute, with its RelativePath and attributes. Emptiness is decided from the ancestors of the file rows the walk already produced, never by re-enumerating each directory, so the pass stays linear in directories plus file rows (the SR-064 discipline). The recorded attributes are Hidden, System, ReadOnly and NotContentIndexed, the only four that can be applied to a directory: Archive, Temporary and Offline are meaningless on one, and Compressed, Encrypted, ReparsePoint and the ReFS integrity bits cannot be set that way at all. Rows sort ordinally, so two runs over the same state write byte-identical sidecars. The directory sidecar (DIRECTORIES.csv) is written beside the index after the index, and is removed when there are no rows, so a tree with no empty or attributed directory is byte-identical to a store without the feature. The prior sidecar is copied into staging so a snapshot keeps its own point in time; it is deliberately not in the kit-artifact list. Both restorers apply it LAST, after every file is written and verified: directories are created parents first and attributes applied deepest first, path traversal is refused as it is for index rows, and the shell restorer creates the directories but reports the Windows attributes as inapplicable on POSIX rather than dropping them silently. cells.Detail: Copying a content group's object is retried in attempt rounds: each round tries every member of the group, then waits and retries the whole list. The waits are 250 ms and then 1000 ms, so three attempts cost at most 1.25 s of waiting per file. Only the refusal to write onto a directory at the destination is treated as permanent, since waiting cannot change it; every other failure is treated as possibly transient, because guessing wrong that way costs time while guessing wrong the other way costs the file. The destination is cleared between rounds, so a retry never lands on or merges into partial debris (SR-004). The retry budget belongs to the set: one budget per set is shared by every group, so a systemically unreadable tree cannot sleep the run away; a direct call without a budget gets a fresh local one. On exhaustion the error names the attempt count and states that the file is NOT in the backup; no row is added for it, and the run is marked unsuccessful. A row from an EARLIER run survives untouched, the same frozen-row treatment SR-055/SR-057 give a file the walk could not read.

cells.Detail: The object-name codec encodes hex to base-57 and refuses an encoding wider than its field rather than keeping the rightmost characters, because a truncated name cannot be checked against the index it addresses. The retired-grammar test is a positive test, never the negation of the first, so a damaged DataPath stays repairable rather than being taken for a legacy store. The shell restorer carries only the retired-grammar predicate (structural; it uses no decoded value) and no current-grammar predicate, which would be dead weight in a file bundled into every backup, since the pool locator matches content rather than names. cells.Detail: The staging-lock ownership helpers belong to the backup-only engine, not the shared library: the library is bundled into every restore kit, so a change there would move both kit-revision markers, and staging-lock ownership has no restore-side meaning. The rule is a dependency direction (the library must not depend on the engine), not a demand that engine concepts move down. Owner record: a once-only JSON payload (SchemaVersion, Kind, a fresh-GUID RunId, set name, host, container id, boot id, pid, StartedUtc, HeartbeatIntervalSeconds, StaleAfterSeconds 1800) written DIRECTLY to RUN.inprogress by a create-new open: one kernel operation that both creates the file and proves exclusivity, with no temporary file and no rename. A temporary write plus a non-overwriting rename is check-then-rename on Unix and so not exclusive there, its atomic variant needs hard links that exFAT lacks, and a crash mid-publish would strand a temporary file in a folder the run may no longer own, which every later classification would read as HoldsContent, a permanent wedge. The record is written only after the staging area was created successfully; a create-new collision is lock-lost, and the caller aborts touching nothing. Torn reads stay safe on the reader side: ParseInvalid with a fresh modification time classifies OwnerLive and refuses. Every marker read goes through one share-tolerant reader, so the heartbeat's open handle cannot make the engine's own fence and classifier reads fail. A read returns its state (Parsed, ParseInvalid or Unreadable), the record, its last-write time and its age; ParseInvalid with the time fields populated is a normal, expected answer (a torn record is exactly a dead writer), while Unreadable is distinct and refuses upstream. The classifier is PURE of I/O decisions: it takes the caller's forced, fail-closed listing and the record and returns one of Empty, EmptyFresh, OwnerStale, OwnerLive, PruneHeld, HoldsContent or Indeterminate, so the whole matrix can be exercised with no filesystem. The roughly 90 s confirmation sample belongs to the caller (LLR-017), which is what keeps the classifier pure. Heartbeat: the beat runs on its own timer, independent of the run's pipeline, so a long hash cannot starve it and a beat can never terminate the process. Starting it performs ONE synchronous beat before the timer is armed and refuses when that touch did not land: a store that rejects setting a modification time would otherwise beat into an unseen error, and after StaleAfterSeconds a live run would read as dead and be confirmed dead, because the confirmation sample detects change and nothing changes. The running heartbeat is kept reachable for the lock's whole lifetime, because an unreachable timer can be collected and stop silently, and nothing else would report it. Each beat re-reads the marker and touches it only when the RunId is its own, holding one open handle across the check and the touch and setting the time through that handle, so the touch lands on the very file the identity check verified; checking and then touching by path would let a reclaim landing between the two freshen the successor's marker. Stopping it reports the error count and last error when either is nonzero (a beat that fails mid-run cannot be made fatal but must not be invisible); it is idempotent, does not throw on a cleanup path, and DRAINS: it cancels, disposes the timer and waits out any in-flight beat, so no touch can land after Stop returns. The reclaim protocol these helpers serve has an exact order: (1) classify, with the confirmation sample on the stale branches; (2) move the staging area aside to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>, refusing on failure with no retry loop; (3) create a fresh staging area and IMMEDIATELY publish the new record, refusing on either failure and leaving the aside folder; (4) re-list the aside folder forced and fail-closed, delete the exact marker by name and then the folder non-recursively, keeping the folder on anything else, any I/O error, or either delete failing. Step 4 is the safety proof, not belt and braces: a frozen-then-resumed owner can write between steps 1 and 2, and a non-recursive delete is structurally incapable of taking a data file with it. The fence points are the FIVE phase boundaries of a backup run (before the staging index write, before eviction, before preserving superseded data, before the backup root's index publish and before the snapshot publish), where a marker whose RunId differs means the lock was lost and the run aborts cleaning up nothing; an unreadable marker is first retried three times about 300 ms apart. The staging OS lock (LLR-090) is a separate primitive and changes nothing here: the classifier is never told whether that lock is held, so holding it can never turn a verdict into a reclaimable one.

cells.Detail: The probe and the storage-form decision belong to the backup-only engine, never the shared library: the library is bundled into every restore kit, so placing them there would move both kit-revision markers for a concept restore has no use for, and the architectural rule is a dependency direction (the library must not depend on the engine), not a demand that engine concepts move down. Probe. The probe opens the source read-only, sharing reads only, the same sharing the hashing and stored-form reads use, so a successful probe predicts a successful copy. It returns 'no measurement' for any path it cannot open; that is a normal, expected answer, not an error. What that sharing buys is platform-qualified. On Windows a read-shared open fails while any writer holds the file, so the probe cannot sample a file open for writing. On POSIX file sharing is advisory, so a non-cooperating writer can change bytes under the sample; against that, and against a Windows writer that opens after the probe does, the probe reads the file's length and last-write time before and after sampling and returns 'no measurement' if either moved. The worst case is the list's answer. Geometry: with 256 KiB windows and three samples, a file shorter than three windows is read once, whole, as a single sample, which avoids over-reading files between 256 KiB and 768 KiB; otherwise three windows are taken at offsets 0, (len - 256 KiB) / 2 (rounded down) and len - 256 KiB, each filled completely unless end of file is reached first. Each window is compressed into a counting sink and its compressed size is read only after the encoder is closed, because a count taken earlier reads short and would call random bytes compressible. The probe reports the sampled and compressed byte totals plus the per-window ratios for the log line. An empty file is below the floor and never probed. Decision. The storage-form decision is a pure function with no I/O. Its inputs are: compression enabled, the set's CompressProbe mode (off, excluded-extensions or always), the already-compressed list's opinion (taken as if compression were enabled, so it carries only the list's view), the length, the size floor, the sampled and compressed byte counts, and the threshold. It returns whether to compress and a Reason in {CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible, ProbeIncompressible}, evaluating SR-081's ordered rule. There is no name-based override, so no input and no Reason is named after a format. Compression disabled is tested FIRST, and with it nothing is read at all. The ruled defaults are held in the engine: a file must shrink by at least 10 percent in aggregate (compressed / original <= 0.90) to be compressed, and files below 256 KiB are never probed. Neither is configurable (SR-081: two knobs nobody can measure), and the shared library exposes neither. Use. The set's CompressProbe value reaches the group copy; a direct call without it uses the default. The decision is made lazily and once per group (LLR-058). Deduplication hits and same-run twins never reach the write path and never probe, which is how SR-061 stays true: no already-stored object's form is ever re-decided. When it does decide, the probe walks the group's candidates, the owner first and then every member (the same list the copy uses, because a locked owner must not fail a group that a readable twin can serve), and samples the first that opens. Only when none opens is the decision ProbeUnavailable, which takes the list's answer with one WARN and never fails the run. Emission: one DEBUG line per written group, 'compress-decision: <rel> <Reason> ratio=<aggregate> windows=<r1,r2,r3>', and three per-set physical-object counters, incremented only after a successful write: 'Probe stored raw: <n> objects, <bytes>', 'Probe compressed: <n>', 'Probe reads: <bytes>'. Codec: Brotli at its fastest level, chosen because it made the fewest wrong decisions against the real whole-file 7-Zip -mx=9 outcome on a calibration corpus, and is also cheaper per sample than Deflate. Deflate's 32 KiB history cannot see a 64 KiB repetition even inside one 256 KiB sample, so it would store raw a file 7-Zip shrinks to nothing. A repetition period longer than a sample window cannot be seen by any codec; that is a limit of sample size and count, and its cost is one file stored raw that could have shrunk, a correct storage form either way (I-1), never a data risk. The decision rule is codec-agnostic.

cells.Detail: The staging OS lock is the file Temp.lock in the change root. Taking it opens the file, creating it if absent, with read access and no sharing: refusing all sharing IS the lock, and read-only access means a read-only attribute cannot wedge it. Any failure to open is retried up to 3 times, 250 ms apart, and then refused with a message beginning [SR-075/lock-held]. The platform error only chooses the wording (held by another process, or could not be opened); every branch refuses identically. The message does not use the lost-marker-lock prefix, so it is never mistaken for a lost marker lock. Releasing closes the file, makes a second release a no-op, accepts a lock that was never taken, never throws and never deletes the file. A test seam inside the same open guard stands in for an open failure. The lock belongs to the backup-only engine, which is not part of the restore kit.

cells.Detail: A backup run's opening order is: resolve the set's paths, creating missing roots; take the staging OS lock; read the prior state; create the run log; then set up staging. No read of store state precedes the lock. If the lock cannot be taken, the run appends one refusal line to the set's backup log (appending, never truncating, because the log belongs to the live holder), marks the set failed and returns. The prior-state reads (the last backup time, the guard against a populated index with no last backup time, and the witness gate) keep their order and run under a guard that releases the lock and re-raises the ORIGINAL error, so the witness refusal still maps to exit 3 and the backup log is left as the last run wrote it. Creating the run log is guarded the same way. Staging setup receives the held lock and passes it to reclaim, which only logs that a current-version holder is excluded and that an older FileBackup takes no OS lock; classification, the confirmation sample and the refusals are untouched (SR-086). If staging setup fails, the lock is released first. Otherwise the lock is released in the run's final cleanup, after the heartbeat is stopped and in a way that cannot be skipped; on the healthy path that is after the snapshot is published, run state is written, deduplication and the browse view run, and it also runs on every error and every lock-lost return. Test seams sit right after the marker is deleted and on either side of the snapshot-publishing rename.

cells.Detail: Storage-form repair and the kit refresh hold the same staging OS lock. Taking it for them refuses a blank change root, creates a missing one, and then takes the OS lock; on any failure it logs one ERROR line through the caller's logger and refuses with a message carrying [SR-075/lock-held]. Repair takes it as its FIRST act, before the storage-form audit, so findings and repair see one state; the kit refresh takes it before listing the snapshots. Both skip it under -WhatIf, and both release it in a final cleanup around their whole body. The lock lives in the mutating operations, not in the verify entry point, so a direct module caller is covered; the verify entry point turns the refusal into exit code 2. A read-only -Action Verify runs only the storage-form audit and the pool-resolution check and takes no lock. Left lock-free because they do not write the store: -Action Snapshots, -Action View (it writes only the view root, which the SR-063 rails keep outside both roots), the -Deep audit (its scratch files are under the system temporary directory) and both restorers (they write only the restore target). Every other engine step that writes the store is a backup or prune step reached only from a backup run or a prune; several of those steps can also be called directly as module exports, and such a direct caller holds no lock.
